questions.prompt: What is the most accurate production review note for a new index?

options.label: Indexes are read-only metadata, so they do not affect writes.
An index is a maintained read structure that must justify write and storage cost.
An index stores complete query results for every common filter.

questions.explanation: A useful index accelerates matching query shapes, but inserts, updates, deletes, storage, and maintenance now pay for it.

questions.prompt: Fill the index design term for composite B-tree ordering.
questions.template: A composite B-tree is most useful when the query constrains the {{blank}} columns in index order.
questions.explanation: An index on account_id, created_at is strongest when account_id participates in the predicate before created_at ordering or range work.

questions.prompt: Order a safe index review flow.

items.label: Account for write and maintenance cost
Verify with the real plan and workload

questions.explanation: Index work should start from a query, then validate whether the read benefit outweighs the operational cost.

questions.prompt: Match each index family to its usual production use.

pairs.match: block summaries for physically correlated data

questions.explanation: The access method should match the shape of the value and the operator family used by the query.

questions.prompt: When is a partial index most likely to help?

options.label: The hot query always includes a predicate that selects a small stable subset.
The query predicate changes on every request and cannot imply the index predicate.
The team wants hundreds of partial indexes instead of partitioning.

questions.explanation: A partial index works when the query's WHERE condition implies the index predicate and the subset is meaningfully smaller.

questions.prompt: Order the debugging path when a new index is not being used.

items.label: Check whether the query predicate matches the index expression or predicate
Check whether the filter returns too much of the table
Check statistics and real EXPLAIN ANALYZE output

questions.explanation: A mismatch in query shape is the first thing to rule out before blaming the planner.
